content.comment_body: Hello, 1) Can the set point for a PI block be linked to the output of a separate function? 2) Alternatively, is it possible to provide the set point for a PI block through a different memory location, such as a flag? I'm aiming for a time-dependent set point that users can easily change, without accessing block settings. Is this achievable? I'm currently using [product_name] with [article_no], but could upgrade to newer [article_no] models if needed. Thanks!
Yes, this can be done. Using an analog multiplexer allows you to achieve this.

analysis.insight_summary: The user wants to adjust the set point of a PI controller block on a [product_name] device, seeking to have the set point driven by another block's output or a designated memory location rather than setting it directly in parameters. The reply confirms this is possible by employing an analog multiplexer, demonstrating that flexible and dynamic set point assignment is supported. The user is focused on enabling easy set point changes for end users, without the need for detailed menu navigation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to be able to change the PI controller's set point dynamically from external sources, preferably through a simple and user-friendly method.
